description: Drift ruleset. One LLM-evaluated rule (agents/drift_reasoning.py) against real pre-computed statistics (agents/drift_stats.py: baseline-vs-comparison PSI, z-score, frequency, mix breakdown) — no hardcoded threshold decides drift, same design as the Log ruleset. Below min_total_transactions, DriftAgent.review() reports insufficient_baseline instead of calling the model at all.

rules.description: The agent's behavior in the comparison window (everything after the first baseline_window_days of visible history) has shifted meaningfully from its own established baseline — average transaction size, frequency, and/or counterparty/category mix — even though no single transaction breaches the mandate. This is case-006's defect: baseline avg ₾187.95 (14 tx, June) vs comparison avg ₾316.51 (35 tx, July-August), z-score 7.15, counterparty-mix PSI 5.86, MCC-mix PSI 2.02 (both far past the conventional 0.25 'major shift' threshold) — a brand-new vendor (Batumi Express Freight) and a brand-new category (vehicle maintenance, MCC 7538) both entering the mix.
rules.notes: PSI/z-score are computed deterministically (agents/drift_stats.py) and handed to the model as real evidence, not a conclusion — whether the shift is meaningful drift (vs. e.g. legitimate seasonal or business-growth variation) is the model's judgment, same design choice as the Log ruleset's structuring rule.
